picks.blurb: THOMAS HUGHES: Virginia Tech has an opportunity to turn a promising start into a true renaissance Friday night. Pitt presents a challenge on defense, and the Hokies will need to help Ethan Grunkemeyer avoid spending the evening under pressure. Quick throws to Luke Reynolds and a productive rushing attack should be central to that effort, and they should be more available than in last Saturday's rainy affair in Chestnut Hill. BLACKSBURG, Va. — Virginia Tech football takes on Pitt tomorrow night in its fifth contest of the 2026 season. Ahead of the Friday evening clash against the Panthers, three members of our staff offered their thoughts on what could unfold tomorrow: JACKSON CAUDELL: This is the biggest Virginia Tech game in years. If they win, they will be 5-0 and have a win against one of the teams expected to compete for a spot in the ACC Championship game, giving them a huge tiebreaker. You could argue that the winner of this game is going to be in the best position to make it to Charlotte and likely face Miami . I expect this to be a close game, but the home-field advantage and Virginia Tech's defense are going to be the difference. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 20 JAMES DUNCAN: Nobody has scored on Pitt in the first or third quarter this season. The Panthers allow 8.5 points per game, fewest in the ACC. Against a Virginia Tech line missing left tackle Justin Terry, I don't see the Hokies hanging 40. Expect quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer to live on quick throws to tight end Luke Reynolds. But Pitt has been flagged 37 times for 359 yards, all at home. Now its first road trip is Lane Stadium on a Friday night. If pre-snap penalties have been an issue at home, who knows what it will be in front of 65,000 people screaming at the top of their lungs when trying to hear a snap count. I still expect this game to come down to the final snap. In fact, I’m predicting a walk-off field goal from John Love to give James Franklin his signature moment in his first season at Virginia Tech. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 24, Pitt 21 Still, I trust Virginia Tech to find enough offense to keep this game within reach throughout. The bigger question is whether the Hokies can force Pitt into the mistakes that become increasingly costly in a close conference matchup. Lane Stadium should have something to say about that, particularly if the Panthers struggle with penalties. I expect a competitive game that remains undecided into the fourth quarter, but that Virginia Tech’s defense delivers the final stop to keep James Franklin’s team unbeaten and firmly in the ACC conversation. picks.blurb: The Penn State transfer has largely handled that responsibility well. Grunkemeyer has completed 101 of 136 passes for 1,012 yards, eight touchdowns and no interceptions through four games. Boston College limited him to 147 passing yards, but the weather played a significant factor. Friday also represents something Pitt hasn't experienced this season: a road game. The Panthers played each of their first four contests at Acrisure Stadium and now head into a sold-out Lane Stadium for a primetime matchup. BLACKSBURG, Va. — For the first time in 20 days, Virginia Tech football hosts a game at Lane Stadium — this one against Pitt with a 5-0 start hanging in the balance. Both the Hokies (4-0, 1-0 ACC) and Panthers (4-0, 1-0 ACC) enter Friday night's contest with unblemished marks, making the matchup one of four games nationally this week between undefeated FBS teams. For Virginia Tech, a victory would secure its first 5-0 start since 2005 and continue a remarkable turnaround in James Franklin's first season at the helm. Virginia Tech's perfect record hasn't come without adversity. After opening the season with commanding victories over VMI (73-3) and Old Dominion (44-21), the Hokies survived consecutive road tests against Maryland and Boston College . Tech defeated the Terrapins 35-26 before escaping a rain-soaked Chestnut Hill with a 21-14 victory. The latter required Virginia Tech to overcome a 14-6 fourth-quarter deficit. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led an 80-yard touchdown drive that ended with a 14-yard score to Marlion Jackson, and Jeffrey Overton Jr. broke free for a 76-yard touchdown less than three minutes later to put the Hokies ahead for good. Overton's emergence has added another dimension to an offense that relied heavily on Grunkemeyer through the first three weeks. The sophomore enters Friday with 409 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 60 carries, averaging 6.8 yards per attempt. He erupted for a career-high 209 yards on 25 carries against Boston College, earning ACC Running Back of the Week honors. Finding similar success against Pitt, though, will be difficult. The Panthers enter Blacksburg allowing just 53.3 rushing yards per game and 8.5 points per contest. Pitt's defense has surrendered just 34 points through four games, following a 59-14 win over Miami (Ohio) with victories of 12-7 over UCF, 27-13 over Syracuse and 59-0 over Bucknell. That creates perhaps the game's most important matchup. Virginia Tech has found a potential difference-maker in Overton, but Pitt possesses one of the stingiest rushing defenses in the country. If the Panthers can prevent Overton from consistently reaching the second level, more responsibility will fall back onto Grunkemeyer. Skip to main content SI.COM The player availability report, which was first used 2025 season, provides five types of designations: available, probable, questionable, doubtful and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Probable corresponds to "likely to play", offering roughly a 75% chance, per the ACC's explanation. Questionable means "uncertain to play", offering around a 50% chance, while doubtful corresponds to unlikely (25%). Out means the player will not play in the game, while a game-time decision (on game day only) means that the final decision will be made closer to the game itself. It's the second straight week that Virginia Tech has 13 players on the availability report: two are out, nine are questionable and two are probable. Five on the report are wide receivers, while there's five offensive linemen, one running back, one corner and one defensive lineman. That was the case leading into last weekend's battle at Boston College. There was a lot of moving around, and Montavious Cunningham missed the game after suffering an injury last week, but at his weekly press conference on Monday, Franklin sounded like someone who was fairly confident that he might be getting some injured players back against Pittsburgh on Friday night. home.headline: Virginia Tech football's initial injury report brings both good and bad news
home.blurb: On Tuesday, the initial availability report for the Pitt game was released. Greene and Cunningham were listed as probable, while Terry was listed as out, something that wasn't a surprise after Franklin's comments on Monday . According to David Cunningham of Tech Sideline , Brody Meadows and Cunningham were participants in practice on Tuesday, but did not go through the one-on-ones against the defense. That is a sign that, despite being listed as probable, Cunningham might not go this week against the Panthers either. It's a short week for the Virginia Tech football team after they rallied in the fourth quarter for a 21-14 win last Saturday afternoon at Boston College. Trailing 14-6, the Hokies scored on back-to-back drives late for their first ACC win under James Franklin. The short week means everything moves up a day, including gameday to Friday night, when Virginia Tech hosts Pittsburgh in a battle of two 4-0 teams at Lane Stadium . Franklin and his staff are dealing with some injuries a third of the way through the season, and the initial availability report for Friday night's game was released, and it brought some promising news for the Hokies. Initial availability report brings mixed news for Virginia Tech vs. Pitt Last week, the Hokies were thin on offense. The week before, against Maryland, offensive lineman Justin Terry went down with an injury in the second quarter; wide receiver Ayden Greene did, too. Then, before the Hokies flew to Boston, offensive lineman Montavious Cunningham popped up on the injury report. That would be a big loss of a veteran lineman ahead of one of the biggest games in Blacksburg in years. That would force Franklin and offensive line coach Matt Moore to shuffle more for the game, and likely during it as well. That's less than ideal. As far as Greene goes, it sounds promising that he could play against Pitt, and that would be big for quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer and offensive coordinator Ty Howle. If not, Marlion Jackson should get more reps after he played against BC and hauled in a fourth-quarter touchdown reception that eventually led to a tie game after Jeffrey Overton Jr. added the two-point conversion. There are still a couple more days before kickoff, and the true test will be pregame warmups on Friday night. Coaches want every possible advantage they can get before game day arrives, so handing out information on which of their players could or could not play is somewhat of an immediate disadvantage, because it lets the other team plan accordingly, and personnel is everything in football. In the latest student-athlete availability report for Boston College football's first conference game of the season, which is against Virginia Tech on Saturday in the wake of an impending Nor'easter that could bring heavy winds and sideways rain to Chestnut Hill, Mass., the Eagles have a relatively high number of injuries entering the contest, the majority of which are categorized as fully "out." The players in that category who were just recently injured would be tight ends Brady Clough and Bryce Lewis, defensive back Cameron Martinez, linebackers Bodie Kahoun and Justin Medlock , and defensive tackle Chris Marable Jr., all of whom played in BC's first two games of the year before sitting out against Maine last Saturday. Now in the "doubtful" category is defensive back Syair Torrence, who is slowly making his return from a season-ending injury he sustained just two games into his redshirt-freshman campaign last year. "It's all about health," O'Brien said of the reason he played mostly on special teams. "He's one of our best players. It has nothing to do with anything other than his health. Whether it was coming back from the knee, which was a serious knee injury, or some soft-tissue stuff he's dealing with. But yeah, once he's really 100 percent healthy, he'll [be out there]. He practiced today, so we'll see how it goes for Saturday." On the bright side, defensive end Kris Jones - one of the best pass rushers on the team - is listed as "questionable," and defensive lineman Onye Nwosisi is in the "probably" category. Nwosisi made his season debut last week against Maine and totaled three tackles and two quarterback hits, so his availability is quite massive. As the team gets ready for the Wildcats, the Nittany Lions will need to make sure that they don't overlook them. Northwestern has played much better to start the season than they have in year's past, opening the year 2-1 under head coach David Braun. For Penn State, this can be a bounce-back game, with the team getting things right after the tough loss against Wisconsin. But Friday night games can be tough, especially having to go on the road. Heading into the game, the Nittany Lions are favored to win the contest, but not by too much. According to ESPN , Penn State is being given a 55.9 percent chance to take down Northwestern on the road. If the Nittany Lions are going to win this game, everything starts and end with quarterback Rocco Becht . Coming over from Iowa State with head coach Matt Campbell, Becht gives Penn State a legitimate option under center. But he has bene prone to some inconsistency at times during his career, and last week was one of those moments for him. Northwestern has its own star quarterback in Aidan Chiles , who transferred to the team this offseason. So far, Chiles has played very well for the Wildcats, throwing for 807 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions. If Penn State can find a way to slow him down, it could make life much easier to grab the win. But Chiles has turned this offense around, and this will be something that the Nittany Lions will need to focus on throughout the game. Overall, Penn State needs to take down Northwestern if they want a chance to make the College Football Playoff this year. away.blurb: Penn State and Northwestern both put out their final Big Ten weekday availability reports before game day on Thursday night. What did we learn about Matt Campbell’s and David Braun’s teams 24 hours before the Nittany Lions clash with the Wildcats at 8 p.m. ET Friday on FOX? Starting with the visitors, top cornerback Daryus Dixson is still questionable. The second-year Nittany Lion appeared on Tuesday’s first report of the week as questionable. Speaking Wednesday morning, Campbell said that would be the case on that night’s report, and it indeed was. Beyond that, there is no other new news for the Lions. Kickoff specialist Cristiano Rosa is out and will not travel to Evanston. Lucas Tenbrock or Ryan Barker will handle kickoffs. Cornerback Christian Askew and linebacker Cam Smith are in the same boat. Top tight end Luke Dehnicke is now doubtful for the Wildcats. He’s a key part of their offense, so it’s obviously not good news for Northwestern. No. 2 receiver Hayden Eligon II is now probable, which is good news, of course. Top defensive back Braden Turner , who did not play last week, is also now doubtful as well. Another key cornerback, Josh Fussel , is now out. Another defensive back to monitor, Damon Walters , is now doubtful for Friday’s game. Last but not least, defensive tackle Troy Regovich could return to action. He is questionable. Most weeks, that will be Wednesday-Friday for head coach Matt Campbell’s team before a Saturday game. However, since this contest is Friday at 8 p.m. ET on FOX, the reports started on Tuesday. The final one then comes out two hours before kickoff. Northwestern is calling top tight end Luke Dehnicke questionable. The same goes for No. 2 receiver Hayden Eligon II and two of the team’s top tacklers, defensive backs Braden Turner and Damon Walters . More notable is that one of the team’s top corners, Josh Fussell , is doubtful to play. Now, Alabama is preparing for its most difficult test yet , as the Crimson Tide are heading on the road to battle the upstart Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday. Like Alabama, Mississippi State is 4-0, and the Bulldogs are also fresh off of a very impressive victory, having topped Missouri last weekend. Mississippi State boasts an explosive offense, and while its defense certainly isn't among the best, it has a pair of terrific cornerbacks in Kelley Jones and Jett Jefferson that could pose some problems for Keelon Russell and Co. So, are the Crimson Tide on upset alert heading into Week 5? A victory would absolutely comprise Alabama's most impressive of the campaign to date and would set Kalen DeBoer's squad up very nicely as it continues to proceed into the most challenging part of its schedule, which begins with the clash against the Bulldogs. While the Crimson Tide are undefeated, things haven't necessarily been easy for them thus far. Alabama took care of business without breaking a sweat against East Carolina in its season opener, but it trailed Kentucky 17-13 at halftime in Week 2 before dominating the second half. It also fell behind Florida State 21-6 in the first half the following week, but ultimately rallied for a 50-36 victory. The Crimson Tide definitely avoided a slow start versus South Carolina last Saturday, taking a 35-3 lead at one point in a 49-18 triumph. One thing is for sure: the version of Alabama that showed up in Weeks 2 and 3 absolutely cannot expect to waltz into Mississippi State and emerge with a victory. The Bulldogs are a significantly better team than either Kentucky or South Carolina, and the Crimson Tide fall behind early, they could be in some serious trouble. Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is one of the top Heisman Trophy candidates at the moment, and the Bulldogs also possess a terrific backfield led by Fluff Bothwell. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has also been a fast riser, too. Alabama cannot mess around this weekend.

away.blurb: Alabama football's initial SEC availability report is out ahead of the Mississippi State game. Right tackle Jayvin James is questionable after leaving Alabama 's home win against South Carolina. James was viewed as "very much questionable" after leaving with a lower-extremity injury late against South Carolina. Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said James is "working through it," and was on the practice field "a little bit." "It's what we expected, the progress he was making," DeBoer said. "Still questionable at this time." Defensive back Zavier Mincey is probable. Both linebackers Justin Hill and Desmond Umeozulu were held out against South Carolina. away.headline: Kalen DeBoer Provides Injury Updates Ahead of Alabama’s Road Trip to Mississippi State
away.blurb: Alabama closed out Saturday's matchup with South Carolina with Mal Waldrep Jr. filling in for William Sanders at left guard and JUCO transfer Tyrell Miller filling in for Jayvin James at right tackle. DeBoer's update on junior William Sanders was encouraging, while senior Jayvin James' status is in more doubt than his offensive line counterpart. "And it just kind of depends on what the week looks like. And then, Jayvin [James], lower extremity. I would say he’s very much questionable at this time. And so, again, we’ll see how the next 24, 48 hours [go]. I think that will help kind of understand what that looks like at the end of the week. But I would say he’s very questionable at this time.” Linebackers Justin Hill (sophomore) and Desmond Umeozulu (senior) both missed Alabama's 49-18 victory over South Carolina with lower-body injuries, and DeBoer said both would continue to miss time, with a more positive update on Hill's eventual return to action. Skip to main content Skip to site footer GET CONNECTED: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. -- On Monday, Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer provided injury updates on six Crimson Tide players, including offensive linemen William Sanders and Jayvin James, who both departed Saturday's win over South Carolina in the second half. "Will [Sanders], upper-body injury during the game. I would expect that he would be able to play on Saturday. So, we’re working through it here, but I would expect that he’ll be ready to go," DeBoer told reporters on Monday. "Both of them will continue to miss some time. Justin will not be as long. Des will be a little further into the season," DeBoer said. "Justin is a lower-extremity, as well as Des. Both happened in the Florida State game. Those guys obviously played valuable snaps for us. Gonna get some other guys to play some snaps that haven’t got as many reps, and other guys that are on the field played more snaps. So, just it’s unfortunate for those guys because they’re playing some good football for us.” Safety Zavier Mincey and offensive lineman Ty Haywood were not spotted dressed during Saturday's win over South Carolina. "Ty is with us. Ty is with us," he said. "Zay just had an injury that popped up during pregame. He was dressed early. He had an injury during pregame there that popped back up. We were expecting him to play, for sure. I would expect he is ready to go this weekend." Haywood, a sophomore from Ryan, Texas, has yet to appear in a game for the Crimson Tide this season after transferring in from Michigan after his freshman season. Mincey, a junior from Daytona Beach, Florida, appeared in the Tide's first two games of the season. picks.headline: Michigan Wolverines vs. Minnesota Gophers Preview and Staff Predictions
picks.blurb: Minnesota is a lot like Iowa. Neither program usually wows you on the offensive side of the ball, but defense and physicality can win them games. Minnesota hasn't quite lived up to expectations since P.J. Fleck was hired, but the Gophers haven't been an easy out when playing in Minnesota. Coming off a game they should’ve won, I expect the Wolverines to come out playing hard. UofM dominated its last game against Iowa, but was held back by being undisciplined with penalties and not being able to finish drives. This being the first road game of the Kyle Whittingham era makes the game closer than it should be, but Michigan will take care of business. Michigan Wolverines vs. Minnesota Gophers Preview and Staff Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM It's not always easy for teams to rebound after a heartbreaking loss. But that's what Michigan is going to attempt to do this weekend after suffering a 20-19 loss to Iowa in Week 4. In reality, Michigan still holds its own fate in its hands . And that starts this weekend. The Wolverines hit the road for the first time and Michigan travels to take on Minnesota . home.blurb: The players listed as OUT for Michigan are the same as Wednesday, and include offensive lineman Andrew Babalola, wide receiver Braydon Alford, running back Micah Ka'apana, running back Jonathan Brown, defensive end Julius Holly and offensive lineman Ace Hamilton. Starting offensive lineman Blake Frazier was listed as PROBABLE for the second day in a row. On Monday, Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham was asked about the statuses of Daley and Blake Frazier. "Not definitive updates for their availability this week," Whittingham said. "It's still early in the week, obviously. So we'll just have to take it day-by-day at this point. There's one or two more things that are going to be assessed or evaluated, and then we should have the clarity we need and whether he's going to become available. Get Jeremiah Smith involved early. Iowa wants to turn this into an ugly, physical Big Ten game where every possession matters. Ohio State can't allow that style to completely dictate the afternoon. Sayin needs to hit a few explosive plays and force Iowa to actually chase points. The Buckeyes also need a much better defensive performance. Illinois finished with 462 total yards last week, including 199 on the ground. If Ohio State gives Iowa the same opportunities, the Hawkeyes can shorten the game and put serious pressure on the Buckeyes late. Kinnick Stadium is going to be insane, and Iowa needs to lean into exactly what it does best: defense, field position, physical football and limiting explosive plays. If the Hawkeyes can keep Smith from completely taking over and force Sayin to consistently execute long drives, this becomes a very different game. And we've already seen Ohio State struggle on the road this season with its loss at Texas. Iowa would love nothing more than to make this another frustrating afternoon away from Columbus. I think Ohio State gets everything it can handle. Iowa's defense slows down the Buckeyes, the crowd makes a legitimate impact and this turns into a fourth-quarter fight. Smith still makes a couple of huge plays, but don't expect another 40-point explosion from Ohio State. Iowa gets the football late with an opportunity to win, but the Buckeyes' defense finally comes up with the stop it needs. Ohio State survives Kinnick — barely. Prediction: Ohio State 21, Iowa 17

picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Picks Florida-Missouri Winner in High-Stakes Week 5 SEC Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM College football analyst Greg McElroy has made his pick for No. 8 Florida at No. 25 Missouri. The ESPN host sees running back Jadan Baugh and the Gators' ground game as the biggest problem for a Tigers team that just lost its conference opener. On his Always College Football podcast , McElroy picked Florida to win 31-24 on Saturday, Oct. 3, at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. "Florida has a deeper offense," he said, "and Missouri's red zone issues, that's something that's difficult to overcome in this game." Florida jumped from No. 21 to No. 8 in the Top 25 poll after a 52-28 win over No. 4 Ole Miss. Missouri slid from No. 19 to No. 25 after it gave up the last 14 points in a 31-24 loss at Mississippi State. "So, for Missouri, this is got-to-have-it mode, given what's coming up here in the next few weeks," McElroy said. McElroy has liked this Florida team since the summer , when he said the Gators could play spoiler in the 2026 Playoff race. How can Missouri slow Jadan Baugh? away.headline: Mizzou injury status for Ahmad Hardy, 2 starting DEs vs Florida on official SEC report
away.blurb: As expected, Mizzou (3-1, 0-1 SEC) will again be without star running back Ahmad Hardy , who opened the week on the Wednesday, Sept. 30, report as "out." The Tigers also listed starting defensive ends Darris Smith and Langden Kitchen as "questionable" for the game against the Gators , which Eli Drinkwitz indicated would be the case during his press conference Tuesday. A questionable designation means neither Smith nor Kitchen have officially been ruled out but will continue to be assessed throughout the week. If Smith can't play, Daeden Hopkins and Jaden Jones are Mizzou's likely starters at defensive end. Smith was helped off of the field during MU's win over Troy this past Saturday. He attempted to return after being evaluated for a lower-body injury in the second half but only lasted one snap before returning to the sideline. Kitchen came off the field during the first quarter of MU's Week 4 game against Mississippi State and was evaluated for a lower-body injury. He did not return to the field. Hardy's timeline for a return after being shot in the upper leg in May is still uncertain. Florida (4-0, 2-0) listed two wide receivers — Vernell Brown III and Bailey Stockton — on the report as questionable. Both players have been involved in the Gators' wideout rotation this year, and Brown leads the team in receiving. For the second straight week, Mizzou also ruled out right tackle Josh Atkins, reserve safety JaDon Blair and backup tight end Gavin Hoffman for this weekend's game. The Tigers added backup linebacker Bobby Washington as "questionable" to face Florida. DE Langden Kitchen (Questionable) LB Bobby Washington (Questionable) WR Vernell Brown III (Questionable) WR Bailey Stockton (Questionable) The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. away.headline: UF injuries: No. 8 Gators hopeful WR Vernell Brown III can play at No. 25 Missouri
away.blurb: GAINESVILLE — Gators coach Jon Sumrall is hopeful leading receiver Vernell Brown III will be available during No. 8 Florida's visit Saturday at No. 25 Missouri. Brown injured his right knee while being tackled on a 6-yard run during the second quarter of Florida's 52-28 win against then-No. 4 Ole Miss. He jogged off the field with a slight limp and did not return while wearing a protective sleeve on his leg. The injury is a low-grade strain, Sumrall said, but Brown's timeline to return is uncertain. Meanwhile, receiver Bailey Stockton will be limited during practice this week. The 5-foot-18, 183-pound Georgia Tech transfer left the Ole Miss game during the first half after he was sandwiched between two tacklers, including safety Joenel Aguero — who was ejected for targeting. “None of those injuries are long-term, catastrophic,” Sumrall said. “All of them, honestly, could be available this weekend.” Florida & Caribbean Experiences Branded Content Paid Partner Content Services About the Orlando Sentinel 🎁 Gift idea: Sentinel's 150th book Sumrall called the injury “nothing serious” and said an MRI did not reveal anything “long term.” “Relative to what you could get, we got great news after the imaging and everything,” Sumrall said Monday. “It’s really going to be as much of a pain tolerance and a confidence with him being ready to go.” “A lot of that’s just how he’s feeling more than anything,” Florida's coach added. “But medically there’s nothing that’s going to hold him other than his own readiness. We got to see how he responds and how he feels ready to go.” The Gators (4-0, 2-0 SEC) did not miss a beat against Ole Miss without Brown. Florida amassed 498 yards and tied the school record for points against a Top 5 foe, matching the 1996 team's scoring total against Florida State during the national title game. An ACC road game is never easy — but the Cavaliers are actually favored to pick up a win at the feared Doak Campbell Stadium. Here are game predictions from the Virginia On SI staff: Jackson Caudell: Virginia 31, Florida State 21 I think this is going to be an interesting test for UVA. While FSU and West Virginia are not the same team, they pose similar challenges. The Seminoles are a mess, but they have talented running backs and a quarterback who can stress you with his legs, much like WVU. Playing away from Charlottesville has not been kind to Virginia so far this year (though a small sample size), and I think they need to be careful here. Most everyone is overlooking Florida State, but they can win this game. However, I have far more trust in Tony Elliott to go on the road and get a win to remain unbeaten in ACC play. Xander Tilock: Virginia 38, Florida State 27 At first glance, I was leaning towards picking the Seminoles at home. However, the other side of the ball is more important, particularly because Florida State has turned the ball over at an average greater than once per game. away.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
away.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. away.blurb: Your Privacy Choices/(Opt-Out of Sale/Targeted Ads) Eagles open conference play at Coastal Carolina with a 1-3 record, plus key injury updates following Saturday’s loss to No. 25 Houston. Georgia Southern is ready to turn the page. The Eagles enter Sun Belt play at 1-3 after dropping three straight games, including Saturday’s 42-28 loss to No. 25 Houston at Allen E. Paulson Stadium. Despite the loss, Georgia Southern showed some encouraging signs offensively. Quarterback Max Johnson turned in his strongest performance of the season, completing 26 of 38 passes for 284 yards and a season-high three touchdowns without an interception. The Eagles also continued to expand the role of quarterback Weston Bryan. Georgia Southern used packages featuring both quarterbacks on the field together, including a flea-flicker that started with Bryan and ended with Johnson finding Alex Taylor for a 40-yard touchdown. Taylor finished with a season-high 119 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Georgia Southern now turns its attention to conference play while also dealing with several injuries. Head coach Clay Helton confirmed Monday that wide receiver Ashton Hollins will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery. Hollins, an Illinois transfer, suffered the injury in the Eagles’ loss at Jacksonville State. Inside linebacker Rashon Myles Jr. also left Saturday’s game against Houston with an Achilles injury. Helton said Myles was scheduled to undergo imaging Monday to determine the extent of the injury. The Eagles were also without two starting offensive tackles against Houston because of illness. Helton said neither had been medically cleared to play. Georgia Southern will now look to regroup as the Sun Belt portion of its schedule begins. The Eagles have lost three straight, while Coastal Carolina enters the matchup at 1-3 and riding a two-game losing streak. Both teams now look for a fresh start, 0-0 in conference play. Saturday will also mark Georgia Southern’s first matchup against the Chanticleers under first-year Coastal Carolina head coach Ryan Beard. The Eagles have won three straight games in the series, including a 26-6 victory in their last trip to Conway in 2024. Georgia Southern leads the all-time series 8-4. Georgia Southern and Coastal Carolina kick off Saturday, Oct. 3, at 7 p.m. from Brooks Stadium in Conway, South Carolina. home.headline: Dabo Swinney provides update on Christopher Vizzina injury, Clemson backup QB plan
home.blurb: Clemson quarterback Christopher Vizzina (right) injured his left elbow against Georgia Southern, but coach Dabo Swinney (left) said Vizzina will still be available vs. North Carolina. Clemson QB Christopher Vizzina is available, coach Dabo Swinney said, but not 100 percent recovered from a small fracture in his left elbow. What’s the Tigers’ plan if they need a backup to play vs. Miami? Clemson listed Vizzina as a game-time decision in the final availability report before Clemson’s Sept. 19 win over North Carolina. He was left off the final report entirely before the Sept. 25 win at Cal. He was listed as Clemson’s backup quarterback on the depth chart vs. Miami, per team release. Top Story Dabo Swinney provides update on Christopher Vizzina injury, Clemson backup QB plan By Jackson Castellano jcastellano@postandcourier.com Jackson Castellano Tigers coach Dabo Swinney said Vizzina is throwing and practicing after sustaining a small left elbow fracture Sept. 12 against Georgia Southern. However, Swinney said that Trent Pearman would be Clemson’s second option at quarterback vs. Miami if necessary. “He's still not 100 percent on his left arm, so if he plays, he plays with a brace on it to protect it,” Swinney said. “But it's really more just the range of motion for him, kind of getting that back fully. But it's gotten a little better each day.” Swinney said Vizzina could play in an emergency. He wasn’t listed in the initial ACC availability report Sept. 30. The senior has 14 completions for 102 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions this season. He was in the running for Clemson’s QB1 job with freshman Tait Reynolds during preseason camp, but Vizzina was ultimately named the starter in Week 1. Vizzina played three drives in the 22-7 win over Georgia Southern before Reynolds took over. The pair had previously split reps in a 51-10 loss to LSU. Reynolds was named the starter moving forward after the Georgia Southern game, but Swinney said the change had nothing to do with Vizzina’s health. In two career starts and four total games, Reynolds has thrown for 521 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Pearman, a fifth-year senior , joined Clemson as a walk-on in 2022. He has 10 passing attempts in his career, completing four for 43 yards. The D.W. Daniel graduate has played 33 career snaps. Reynolds will start for Clemson (3-1, 2-0 ACC) in its Oct. 3 matchup with No. 4 Miami (4-0, 2-0). Reach Jackson Castellano at jcastellano@po

home.headline: What first Miami-Clemson availability report reveals about key Hurricanes injuries
home.blurb: Junior Xavier Lucas , who hasn't played since the season opener against Stanford , is listed as questionable for Saturday, according to the Atlantic Coast Conference's first availability report for the game released on Wednesday. Miami has been playing without three of its top cornerbacks basically all season, with starters Lucas and OJ Frederique out since the Stanford game and sophomore reserve Ja'Boree Antoine out since before the season began. Other players who sat out or were banged up against Central Michigan but don't appear on the availability report: running back Mark Fletcher Jr. , defensive linemen Ahmad Moten Sr. and Armondo Blount, and linebacker Kellen Wiley. Linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin is listed as questionable and reserve tight end Owen Ruskavich is out. As for Clemson, two players are listed as questionable (defensive end Armon Mason and Elyjah Thurmon), while seven have been ruled out (safety Polo Anderson, cornerback Shavar Young Jr., wide receiver Cole Turner , running back David Eziomume, defensive tackles Kourtney Kelly and Markus Strong, and offensive lineman Mason Wade). In their absence, the trio of Ethan O'Connor, Damari Brown and safety Bryce Fitzgerald have been Miami's primary outside cornerbacks. As expected, sophomore tight end Luka Gilbert (undisclosed), redshirt junior running back CharMar “Marty” Brown (right knee), and sophomore wide receiver Joshua Moore (right shoulder) have been ruled out – the case for the rest of the season. Cornerbacks junior Romanas “OJ” Frederique Jr. (left shoulder) and Ja’Boree Antoine (undisclosed) are ruled out for the weekend. Both defenders are expected to return at a later portion of the regular season. Antoine has yet to play and Frederique Jr. has been sidelined since the first drive against Stanford. Newly added to the list, redshirt junior tight end Owen Ruskavich (undisclosed) has been ruled out. He’s logged a new collegiate career high, playing 26 snaps this season. Ruskavich didn’t appear in last Saturday’s 52-3 win over Central Michigan at Hard Rock Stadium. Junior cornerback Xavier Lucas (undisclosed) is listed as questionable. Head coach Mario Cristobal described a return this weekend as “possibly.” Lucas will likely be a game-time decision. The Hurricanes’ secondary has run thin over the last three weeks; a return would add much-needed depth. Sophomore linebacker Ezekiel Marcelin Jr. (undisclosed) is listed as questionable. He has shown promising signs this season. Marcelin Jr. is one of nine Hurricanes defenders with at least 10 tackles, including three solos and seven assists, a tackle for loss, and a forced pressure. Clemson has starting junior left guard Elyjah Thurmon (undisclosed) as questionable. Meanwhile, junior nickelback Corian Gipson and fifth-year defensive tackle Devarrick Woods, who missed last Friday’s 24-10 win over Cal, aren’t listed.
